discovery: Cavity optomechanics: quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion by radiation pressure

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Andrew N. Cleland
nominees.affiliation: Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering, University of Chicago, USA

motivation: The nominees showed that mechanical objects made of billions of atoms can be brought into the quantum regime and controlled at the level of single quanta. Kippenberg and Aspelmeyer, independently and at the same time, showed radiation-pressure sideband cooling of micromechanical resonators. They then reached strong optomechanical coupling, ground-state cooling and coherent quantum control of motion using light. Cleland placed a macroscopic mechanical resonator in its quantum ground state and swapped single phonons with a superconducting qubit, the first quantum control of a mechanical object. Together these works founded cavity optomechanics. They made measurements limited only by quantum back-action and the standard quantum limit, and they reached squeezing and entanglement of mechanical motion. The same ideas now serve as tools: quantum transduction between microwave and optical signals, ultrasensitive force and displacement sensing, and tests of quantum mechanics at macroscopic scales.
